prompts.pose: Hurt recoil, frame 1 of 2: chest and shoulders snap a small distance backward to screen-left, weight on rear planted foot; knees flex slightly. Face still looks right with the exact approved eye shape and opening. Near RIGHT arm stays in front and right hand NEVER lets go of the same shaft grip; staff tilts a few degrees away to screen-right, outside face and body. Far LEFT empty hand balances behind far hip. Hair and hat ornaments lag left from recoil, no effects.
prompts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: ONE clean isolated animation sprite, not a contact sheet. Input image 1 is the ONLY approved identity and scale reference crooked_witch_base_v4_02. Preserve exact face, purple eye outline, silver curled hair, crooked purple-gold hat and ornaments, detailed purple-gold robe with cream ruffles, brown boots and the EXACT SAME crystal staff dimensions. For hurt preserve the precise reference eyelid opening. For KO only, eyelids may close as she collapses. No redesign of eyes.
Canvas 1254x1254 with true transparent alpha. No backdrop or haze of any color, no smoke, no aura, no particles, no ground or shadow. Same camera, pixel-art painted fantasy style, body, head, hat, limbs, boots and staff scale. Keep a right-facing three-quarter side orientation throughout the motion, even when falling sideways. Near RIGHT arm and leg foreground; far LEFT arm and leg behind torso. Near right shoulder/sleeve/elbow/forearm connect naturally to gripping right hand, left hand empty. Same one-handed grip on middle/lower shaft until an explicit release frame. An explicit open-palm release in KO frames 3/4 means the same RIGHT hand releases, not a hand swap; exactly ONE staff remains. Staff never pierces clothing, hair or body. Ground contact baseline stays y1170; crouching and falling move joints and feet anatomically, never by resizing.

Preserve the exact same character identity, body height, head size, shoulder width,
limb proportions, weapon size, camera distance, foot position and lighting as the reference.
Right-facing three-quarter side view, full body and the entire weapon inside the frame,
flat transparent background, no shadow, no text, no border, no scenery.

Centering and framing are positioning choices only: never zoom, scale, stretch or shrink the
character to center it or to fit the full body/weapon. This applies whether the weapon is raised,
lowered or held horizontally. If the weapon makes the silhouette taller or wider, keep the
character and weapon scale fixed and expand the canvas/margins or adjust the framing instead.
If the canonical runtime frame still cannot contain the full weapon at the fixed scale, stop and
ask the user; do not shrink the character or crop the weapon.

Correct near/far layering: the near arm and near leg are in front of the torso; the far arm
and far leg stay behind it. The weapon is held by the same hand with a believable grip around
the haft; fingers wrap the haft, and the hand/weapon do not intersect the torso, head, legs,
hair or clothing. No interpenetration, no merged or extra limbs, no floating parts, and no
duplicated weapon.

Only change the pose: hurt, frame 1 of 2. Hurt recoil, frame 1 of 2: chest and shoulders snap a small distance backward to screen-left, weight on rear planted foot; knees flex slightly. Face still looks right with the exact approved eye shape and opening. Near RIGHT arm stays in front and right hand NEVER lets go of the same shaft grip; staff tilts a few degrees away to screen-right, outside face and body. Far LEFT empty hand balances behind far hip. Hair and hat ornaments lag left from recoil, no effects..

prompts.pose: Hurt recovery, frame 2 of 2: regain upright balance nearly matching base idle, both boots on original ground line, shoulders settle. Near RIGHT arm in front still gripping same point of staff, return staff upright outside the face. Far LEFT empty hand lowers behind far hip. Hair tips and hat charms finish their delayed recoil. Exact same eye shape and opening as approved base, no effects.
